subproblem.title: Besicovitch–Vitali cover of E by disjoint admissible closed balls inside an open set
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → ℝ → Prop) (E W : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → IsOpen W → E ⊆ W → (∀ x ∈ E, ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ ρ < δ ∧ Q x ρ) → ∃ (t : Set (Euclid P)) (r : Euclid P → ℝ), t.Countable ∧ t ⊆ E ∧ (∀ x ∈ t, 0 < r x ∧ closedBall x (r x) ⊆ W ∧ Q x (r x)) ∧ t.PairwiseDisjoint (fun x => closedBall x (r x)) ∧ μ (E \ ⋃ x ∈ t, closedBall x (r x)) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1–3 of the parent proof, together with the inclusion V ⊆ W from its Step 4. Mathematically this is Simon, Ch. 1, Remark 3.11(3): a measure on ℝ^n that is finite on compact sets has the symmetric Vitali property, proved there from the Besicovitch Covering Lemma 3.12. The balls are chosen inside an open set as in the proof of Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.13. Here the parent's integral inequality is replaced by an arbitrary admissibility predicate Q.

1. (Setting.) The hypothesis says μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K, which is exactly IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ. In Lean, register it with `have : IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ := ⟨hK⟩`. ℝ^P is a proper metric space, so every closed ball B̄_k(0), k ∈ ℕ, is compact and has finite μ-measure. Since ℝ^P = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} B̄_k(0), μ is σ-finite and therefore s-finite; on Euclid P, Lean infers the instance SFinite μ from IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ. ℝ^P (Euclid P) is a second-countable metric space whose σ-algebra is the Borel σ-algebra, so open sets are measurable. Being a finite-dimensional real normed space, it has the Besicovitch covering property (Mathlib instance Besicovitch.instHasBesicovitchCovering, file Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Covering/BesicovitchVectorSpace.lean).

2. (Admissible radii.) For x ∈ ℝ^P put f(x) := {ρ ∈ ℝ : B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ W and Q(x, ρ)}. We claim that for every x ∈ E and every δ > 0, f(x) ∩ (0, δ) is nonempty.
- Since x ∈ E ⊆ W and W is open, there is R > 0 with B_R(x) ⊆ W (open ball; Metric.isOpen_iff).
- Since min(δ, R) > 0, the hypothesis gives ρ with 0 < ρ < min(δ, R) and Q(x, ρ).
- As ρ < R, the closed ball B̄_ρ(x) is contained in B_R(x) ⊆ W (closedBall_subset_ball).
Hence ρ ∈ f(x), and since 0 < ρ < δ, ρ ∈ f(x) ∩ (0, δ).

3. (Measurable Besicovitch covering theorem.) Apply Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Covering/Besicovitch.lean). Its arguments are the s-finite measure μ, the radius sets f, the set s := E, and the bound function R ≡ 1, which is positive at every point of E. Its covering hypothesis is exactly the claim of Step 2. No measurability of E is required. It gives a set t ⊆ ℝ^P and a function r : ℝ^P → ℝ such that:
- t is countable and t ⊆ E;
- r(x) ∈ f(x) ∩ (0, 1) for every x ∈ t;
- μ(E ∖ ⋃_{x∈t} B̄_{r(x)}(x)) = 0;
- t is pairwise disjoint for the family x ↦ B̄_{r(x)}(x).

4. (Unpacking.) Let x ∈ t. Since r(x) ∈ (0, 1), we have 0 < r(x). Since r(x) ∈ f(x), we have B̄_{r(x)}(x) ⊆ W and Q(x, r(x)). This gives (a). The pairwise disjointness from Step 3 is (b), and the null-set statement from Step 3 is (c). Together with the countability of t and t ⊆ E, the pair (t, r) has every required property. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ finite on compacts gives IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ, hence μ is σ-finite and s-finite. Euclid P is second countable and Borel, and has the Besicovitch covering property (instHasBesicovitchCovering).
Admissible radii f(x) := {ρ : closedBall x ρ ⊆ W ∧ Q x ρ} meet every (0, δ) for x ∈ E. Take an open ball B_R(x) ⊆ W and apply the hypothesis with min(δ, R).
Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae with s = E and R ≡ 1 gives: t countable, t ⊆ E, r(x) ∈ f(x) ∩ (0,1), pairwise disjoint closed balls, and an uncovered part of E of measure zero.
Unpack r(x) ∈ f(x) ∩ (0,1) into 0 < r x, closedBall x (r x) ⊆ W and Q x (r x).

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean proposition agree, including arbitrary Q and nonmeasurable E. Compact finiteness supplies SFinite; shrinking by min(δ,R) puts admissible closed balls inside W. The pinned Besicovitch theorem supplies every stated conclusion without measurability of E. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and siblings.

subproblem.title: Bounding the integral over W from a bound on a measurable subset V and |g| ≤ 1
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P, and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |g(x)| ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. x. Let θ ∈ ℝ, and let V ⊆ W ⊆ ℝ^P with V measurable, W arbitrary and μ(W) < ∞. If ∫_V g dμ ≤ θ·μ(V), then ∫_W g dμ ≤ μ(W) − (1 − θ)·μ(V). All measures are read as real numbers via ENNReal.toReal, and set integrals are taken with respect to the restricted measure μ⌞S (μ.restrict S).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (θ : ℝ) (V W : Set (Euclid P)), AEStronglyMeasurable g μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, |g x| ≤ 1) → MeasurableSet V → V ⊆ W → μ W < ∞ → ∫ y in V, g y ∂μ ≤ θ * (μ V).toReal → ∫ y in W, g y ∂μ ≤ (μ W).toReal - (1 - θ) * (μ V).toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 and the first part of Step 7 of the parent proof (∫_W g = ∫_{W∖V} g + ∫_V g ≤ μ(W) − μ(V) + θ·μ(V)), stated for an arbitrary measurable V ⊆ W. All measures are read as real numbers via ENNReal.toReal. For an arbitrary set S, ∫_S g dμ is the integral with respect to the restricted measure μ⌞S, whose total mass is μ(S).

1. (Finiteness.) By monotonicity, μ(V) ≤ μ(W) < ∞ and μ(W ∖ V) ≤ μ(W) < ∞.

2. (Integrability.) For every set S, the hypothesis |g| ≤ 1 μ-a.e. implies ‖g‖ = |g| ≤ 1 μ⌞S-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae). Since g is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, g is integrable on every S with μ(S) < ∞ (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded with bound 1). In particular, g is integrable on V and on W ∖ V. The constant 1 is also integrable on W ∖ V (integrableOn_const, since μ(W ∖ V) < ∞).

3. (Splitting.) The sets W ∖ V and V are disjoint (disjoint_sdiff_left), V is measurable, and (W ∖ V) ∪ V = W because V ⊆ W (sdiff_union_of_subset). setIntegral_union needs measurability only of the second set V, so it gives ∫_W g dμ = ∫_{W∖V} g dμ + ∫_V g dμ.

4. (Bound on the complement.) μ⌞(W ∖ V)-a.e. we have g ≤ |g| ≤ 1, and both g and 1 are integrable on W ∖ V. By monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono_ae), ∫_{W∖V} g dμ ≤ ∫_{W∖V} 1 dμ = μ(W ∖ V).toReal.

5. (Measure of the difference.) Since V ⊆ W, V is measurable and μ(V) < ∞, measure_sdiff gives μ(W ∖ V) = μ(W) − μ(V) in [0, ∞]. Since μ(V) ≤ μ(W) < ∞, ENNReal.toReal_sub_of_le gives (μ(W) − μ(V)).toReal = μ(W).toReal − μ(V).toReal.

6. (Conclusion.) Combine Steps 3–5 with the hypothesis ∫_V g dμ ≤ θ·μ(V).toReal. By linear arithmetic, ∫_W g dμ ≤ (μ(W).toReal − μ(V).toReal) + θ·μ(V).toReal = μ(W).toReal − (1 − θ)·μ(V).toReal. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ V ≤ μ W < ∞ and μ (W \ V) ≤ μ W < ∞. Since |g| ≤ 1 a.e. and g is a.e. strongly measurable, g is integrable on V and on W \ V (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded).
Split ∫_W g = ∫_{W∖V} g + ∫_V g using setIntegral_union (V measurable, W = (W ∖ V) ∪ V).
(μ (W ∖ V)).toReal = (μ W).toReal − (μ V).toReal by measure_sdiff and ENNReal.toReal_sub_of_le.
Linear arithmetic with ∫_V g ≤ θ * (μ V).toReal.

audit.reason: The exact type matches the prose, including arbitrary W. The global almost-everywhere hypotheses restrict to every set and give the required integrability. Measurability of V alone suffices for setIntegral_union and measure_sdiff; finiteness justifies toReal subtraction. Combining these identities with the complement bound proves the conclusion for arbitrary θ without circularity.

subproblem.title: Summing a set-integral bound over a countable disjoint family of measurable sets
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (θ : ℝ) (t : Set (Euclid P)) (B : Euclid P → Set (Euclid P)), t.Countable → (∀ x ∈ t, MeasurableSet (B x)) → t.PairwiseDisjoint B → μ (⋃ x ∈ t, B x) < ∞ → IntegrableOn g (⋃ x ∈ t, B x) μ → (∀ x ∈ t, ∫ y in B x, g y ∂μ ≤ θ * (μ (B x)).toReal) → ∫ y in ⋃ x ∈ t, B x, g y ∂μ ≤ θ * (μ (⋃ x ∈ t, B x)).toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 of the parent proof, which uses countable additivity of μ and of the integral over the disjoint admissible balls. Here it is stated for an arbitrary countable disjoint family of measurable sets B(x), x ∈ t. Write V := ⋃_{x∈t} B(x). All measures are read as real numbers via ENNReal.toReal.

1. (Reindexing by the subtype.) Since t is countable, the subtype ↥t = {i // i ∈ t} is a countable type (Set.Countable.to_subtype). By Set.biUnion_eq_iUnion, V = ⋃_{i : ↥t} B(i). Each B(i), i : ↥t, is measurable because i ∈ t. The family i ↦ B(i) on ↥t is pairwise disjoint: if i ≠ j in ↥t, their underlying points are distinct (the coercion ↥t → ℝ^P is injective) and both lie in t, so B(i) and B(j) are disjoint by t.PairwiseDisjoint B.

2. (Countable additivity of the integral.) g is μ-integrable on V = ⋃_{i : ↥t} B(i), the index type is countable, and the sets B(i) are measurable and pairwise disjoint. By MeasureTheory.hasSum_integral_iUnion, the real family i ↦ ∫_{B(i)} g dμ has sum ∫_V g dμ (HasSum).

3. (Countable additivity of the measure.) By measure_iUnion, μ(V) = Σ'_{i : ↥t} μ(B(i)) in [0, ∞].
- For every i, μ(B(i)) ≤ μ(V) < ∞ by monotonicity, so every term is finite. By ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq, μ(V).toReal = Σ'_i μ(B(i)).toReal.
- Since Σ'_i μ(B(i)) = μ(V) ≠ ∞, the real family i ↦ μ(B(i)).toReal is summable (ENNReal.summable_toReal). So it has sum μ(V).toReal (HasSum).
- Multiplying by the constant θ (HasSum.mul_left), the family i ↦ θ·μ(B(i)).toReal has sum θ·μ(V).toReal.

4. (Termwise comparison.) For every i : ↥t, the hypothesis at the point i ∈ t gives ∫_{B(i)} g dμ ≤ θ·μ(B(i)).toReal. Two real families with sums that are ordered term by term have ordered sums (hasSum_le). Applied to the sums from Steps 2 and 3, this gives ∫_V g dμ ≤ θ·μ(V).toReal. No sign condition on θ is needed, because both series converge and are compared term by term. If t = ∅, both sides are 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Reindex V = ⋃_{x∈t} B x as ⋃_{i : ↥t} B i over the countable subtype. Measurability and pairwise disjointness carry over.
hasSum_integral_iUnion gives HasSum (i ↦ ∫ y in B i, g y ∂μ) (∫ y in V, g y ∂μ).
measure_iUnion, ENNReal.tsum_toReal_eq and ENNReal.summable_toReal give HasSum (i ↦ (μ (B i)).toReal) (μ V).toReal. Multiply by θ.
hasSum_le with the termwise hypothesis gives ∫ y in V, g y ∂μ ≤ θ * (μ V).toReal.

audit.reason: The type includes exactly the stated countability, measurability, disjointness, finiteness, integrability and termwise bounds. Reindexing by the countable subtype gives both HasSum identities; finite total measure justifies conversion to real sums. Termwise comparison works for arbitrary θ, including negative θ. No missing hypothesis or circular dependence remains.
